solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: SOS minibus put out admitting defeat

indicators.note: put out in the sense of disordered or upset, so the letters of the two words get rearranged

explanation.surface: A distress call goes out from a minibus whose passengers have given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' is the anagram signal working on all ten letters of SOS MINIBUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Yielding to an opponent is an act of surrender, the noun form of giving in.

clue.text: Word used to open Home Counties do

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
do is short for ditto, meaning the same again

explanation.surface: An invitation to open a party being held in the counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party but is ditto, the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Ali Baba tale the magic password that makes the robbers' cave open is 'open sesame'.

clue.text: Doing well without arousing interest

definitions.meaning: drilling a well into the ground is the act of making a bore hole
dull, tedious, failing to interest anyone

explanation.surface: Someone is succeeding nicely but fails to excite anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing well' reads as thriving, but here it is making a well with a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Drilling a hole is the verb sense; tedious and dull is the adjective sense of the same word.

clue.text: Something for those willing to pay

definitions.text: Something for those willing to pay

parts.words: Something for those willing to pay
parts.note: willing here means leaving property by a will, so the payment is a levy on an estate passed on at death

explanation.surface: Something offered to people who are prepared to spend money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'willing' seems to mean eager; it means bequeathing by will.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty charged on a dead person's estate falls on what is passed on through a will.

clue.text: Spare chap deployed where he's no longer any use

definitions.text: where he's no longer any use

indicators.note: deployed means arranged or spread out into position, so the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A surplus fellow is sent off to a place where he serves no purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges the letters of SPARE CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thrown on the rubbish pile is the idiom for being discarded as worthless.

clue.text: Fiat runs into European river

indicators.note: into says the runs letter goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Oder flows between Germany and Poland
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Fiat car is driven into a river somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiat' looks like the car maker; it is a decree.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiat is an authoritative command or decree, as is an instruction from above.

clue.text: Countdown 'ost in jug

indicators.note: 'ost is host with its first letter dropped, Cockney style, telling us to drop the H from the host's name too

parts.note: Nick Hewer hosted the British TV word-and-numbers quiz Countdown

explanation.surface: The presenter of a TV quiz is found inside a jug.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British daytime quiz show, once hosted by Nick Hewer; the dropped aitch in 'ost shows the H goes from his name as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A large pitcher with a wide mouth, traditionally used with a washbasin, is a classic jug.

clue.text: King in roadway abused pedestrian …

indicators.note: in places the king letter inside the rearranged road word
abused means mistreated or misused, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king on a roadway abuses someone walking by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abused' rearranges ROADWAY to WORADAY; 'in' puts K inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian as an adjective means dull and ordinary, which is everyday and unremarkable.

clue.text: … jogger on old TV programme

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
Minder was a British TV comedy-drama of the 1980s about a bodyguard

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a runner on an old television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Minder was a popular British series about a minder, a hired bodyguard. The ellipsis joins the two clues as one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that jogs the memory prompts recall, so a memory jogger is a prompt.

clue.text: Spanish resort with jerk about to tell office worker

parts.note: a costa is a Spanish coastal holiday strip, as in Costa del Sol

indicators.note: about means the jerk word goes round the tell word

parts.note: to cant is to tilt or toss with a jerk
to tell is to count, as a teller counts votes

explanation.surface: A clerk on a Spanish holiday, accompanied by an idiot who is about to inform on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like part of 'about to' but is the container signal; 'jerk' is a verb here, to toss or tilt, not an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A clerk who analyses production costs for a business is a type of white-collar employee.

clue.text: Bears returned round ancient city in chapter of the Kuran

indicators.note: round says the reversed word wraps about the city
returned means the bears word is read backwards

parts.note: bears in the sense of has or carries
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in crosswords

explanation.surface: Bears come back to an ancient city, mentioned in a section of the Koran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' tempts towards URSA; it is HAS, turned to SAH by 'returned'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the hundred and fourteen sections of the Muslim holy book is called by this Arabic name.

clue.text: Old piece of furniture making sound diagnostic aid

definitions.text: Old piece of furniture making sound
definitions.meaning: a cabinet combining wireless and record player, popular mid-century
an X-ray picture used by doctors to diagnose

explanation.surface: A vintage cabinet being turned into a reliable aid for doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' seems to mean reliable, but belongs to the first definition: the furniture makes sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio-gramophone cabinet is old-fashioned furniture; the same word is also an older name for an X-ray image.

clue.text: Femme fatale's power after charm used repeatedly

indicators.note: after says the power letter follows the charm

parts.note: a mantra is an incantation chanted over and over
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A seductive woman's hold over men follows from her charm, used again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts come in answer order MANTRA then P, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman who ensnares men is jocularly called a trap set for them.

clue.text: Prepare for new work to keep about right

indicators.note: about tells us the keep word surrounds the right letter

parts.note: to keep is to retain

explanation.surface: Getting ready for a new job while holding on to one's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes RETAIN go round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning fresh skills to change occupation is what being trained again means.

clue.text: It's expensive letting champion put in for gruelling race

parts.note: steep prices are high ones

indicators.note: put in says the champion letters go inside the letting word

parts.note: a lease is a letting of property

explanation.surface: Expensive rentals let a champion enter a tough race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting' is a noun, a rental, not the verb it seems; 'put in' places the champion inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race over fences and ditches is a demanding obstacle event.

clue.text: Pass through Parliament on one group of candidates

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
I is the Roman numeral one
a slate is a list of candidates standing for election

explanation.surface: A bill goes through Parliament on the strength of one party's list of candidates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' = LEG is a cricket convention: the on side and leg side are the same half of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To make laws is the business of a legislature, as when bills are enacted.

clue.text: One starting course menial served up involved ham and trace of nuts

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means the menial word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a serf is a lowly labourer

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the three letters are mixed
a trace of something is a tiny bit of it, here its first letter

explanation.surface: A first course served by a servant: tangled ham with a hint of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns SERF to FRES; 'involved' shuffles HAM to HMA; N is the first letter of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-year university student is beginning a course of study.

clue.text: Defectors not starting to be roughed up without punishment

indicators.note: roughed up means beaten about, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not starting means the word loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Defectors who never got going are beaten up yet get off unpunished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops D, leaving EFECTORS; 'roughed up' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free is the idiom for escaping any penalty or harm.

clue.text: Homer in competition to reform pig-ignorance

indicators.note: to reform is to shape again, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Homer enters a contest to correct the ignorance of pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the poet, or Homer Simpson; it is a homing bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing bird; one flown in timed contests is bred for speed.

clue.text: Bones associated with Italy's foremost Renaissance family

parts.note: Bones is a slang name for a doctor, as Dr McCoy in Star Trek

indicators.note: foremost signals the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Skeletons linked with the leading Italian family of the Renaissance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bones' seems anatomical but is a nickname for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine banking dynasty were great patrons of art in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Quivering like fish

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
the hake is a food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Trembling as a landed fish does.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic adjective means trembling or shaking, a literary synonym for shivering.

clue.text: Models with undemanding goals

definitions.meaning: people who pose for an artist or photographer
easy chances to score in sport, ones that should not be missed

explanation.surface: Fashion models whose ambitions are not very taxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goals' looks like ambitions but means scoring chances, as in football or cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Artists' models pose seated; in sport an easy catch or open goal is called by the same word.

clue.text: Shoot that is getting one charged

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
an ion is an electrically charged atom

explanation.surface: A shooting incident where someone ends up charged by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is a less familiar abbreviation for scilicet, Latin 'namely'; 'Shoot' is the plant sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A young plant shoot, especially one cut for grafting, is a horticultural term also used for an heir.

clue.text: Sombre at first if not gloomy

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: unless means if not, a conditional

explanation.surface: Grave at the start, unless things turn out to be dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: A day without sunshine is dark and dreary, a synonym for gloomy.

clue.text: 'Lovely' girl after a light weight rejected cocktail

indicators.note: after puts the girl's name behind the reversed part
rejected means thrown back, so the words before it are read backwards

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
Lovely Rita is a Beatles song about a meter maid

explanation.surface: A pretty girl turns down a lightweight suitor's cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks point to the Beatles song 'Lovely Rita'; 'rejected' turns back both 'a' and the weight, giving MARGA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila, lime and orange liqueur in a salt-rimmed glass make this classic mixed drink.

clue.text: Creature ultimately lacking soul

indicators.note: ultimately lacking says the word is missing its final letter

parts.note: an animal is a living creature

explanation.surface: A beast that, in the end, has no soul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately lacking' drops the last letter L from ANIMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jungian psychology and Latin, this word means the inner self or spirit.

clue.text: Want work by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says we want a word that sounds like the work word

parts.note: to knead dough is to work it with the hands

explanation.surface: Wanting work, so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the sound of it' looks like 'apparently' but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To want is to require or lack something, a simple synonym.

clue.text: Unable to move having imbibed last of potent drink — get knotted!

indicators.note: having imbibed means the immobile word drinks in, so contains, the following letter

parts.note: inert means motionless, unable to move

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: wine is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Paralysed after downing the dregs of a strong drink, someone is told rudely to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get knotted!' is a British rude dismissal, but read literally it means become knotted. 'having imbibed' puts T inside INERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist strands together is to tangle them, as when they become knotted.
